history.summary: Listed as a 957 sqft '1BR' freehold in Geylang, but the unit is actually a 2BR in a tiny 75-unit Lorong 22 boutique — the low $1,149 psf reflects the oversize and Geylang location, not value. Null URA data, off-frontier, and Geylang-stigma make this a thin-data boutique to avoid on investment grounds.
history.rating_rationale: All URA fields are null, so the inflated score_1000 of 946 is built on neutral-filled blanks rather than evidence, and the listing is off the value frontier. Web check confirms Grandview Suites is a 75-unit freehold boutique on Lorong 22 Geylang, and this 957 sqft unit is a 2BR (misclassified as 1BR) — the cheap PSF is a size/location artifact. A 75-unit dev gives very thin liquidity, the Geylang red-light-district adjacency carries financing and resale stigma for many buyers, and there is no transaction or appreciation data to underwrite an investment case. No verifiable thesis plus stigma equals Avoid.

history.summary: The algo's 928 score and -38.9% 'cheapness' are a data artifact: this 957 sqft 'unit' is a PENTHOUSE mislabeled as a 1-bedroom (Grandview's 1BRs are 355-635 sqft; only its 7 penthouses span 958-2024 sqft). Comparing a penthouse PSF against small-unit PSFs manufactures a fake discount.
history.rating_rationale: Listing is $1,100,000 / 957 sqft = $1,149 psf, flagged 'very_low_psf' and 'bedroom_sqft_mismatch'. Web confirms Grandview Suites (52 units, 2016, FH, Lorong 22 Geylang) has 1BRs of 355-635 sqft and penthouses of 958-2024 sqft, so this 957 sqft 'beds:1' entry is a penthouse. Penthouses structurally trade far below small-unit PSF, so the -38.9% age-adj and -7.7% cohort premium (on psf_cohort_txns=1, a single comparable) are quirks, not value. Recent small-unit transactions print ~$1,540 psf but that is not the right comp. D14 Geylang freehold averages only ~$1,516 psf vs ~$1,706 East region and ~$1,953 islandwide, with the seedy-area stigma and slow price growth; small Geylang projects often see <5 transactions/year, hurting resale valuation.
red_flags: 957 sqft '1-bed' is actually a penthouse - bedroom_sqft_mismatch confirmed against floor-plan data
psf_cohort_txns=1: the -7.7% cohort discount is computed on a single comparable (statistically meaningless)
very_low_psf flag is an artifact of comparing penthouse PSF to small-unit PSF, not a real bargain
Geylang stigma: D14 FH ~$1,516 psf lags East ~$1,706 and islandwide ~$1,953 with slow growth
Thin liquidity: small (52-unit) Geylang developments often transact <5x/yr, weak exit/valuation
catalysts: Walkable to Aljunied (EW9) and Mountbatten (CC7) MRT; abundant F&B and buses
Freehold tenure (not a forward edge per v3.4, but preserves optionality)

agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: appreciation_pct 3.7% is the regional_baseline fallback (not project-realized) over 15 txns; D14 Geylang FH has documented slow growth and more losses than gains, so forward upside is structurally capped. Trailing figure carries ~0 forward power here.
agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Project-level rental yields are cited as healthy (~7.4% on small units), but that applies to 355-377 sqft units, not this penthouse; a large penthouse in a stigmatised small project rents thinly and at lower yield.
